factProposals.value: Outside indexing and search engines (Madison AI) read work orders through a read-only HTTP API at /api/v1: list with cursor paging, changes since a time, keyword search, and get one. Exercised with a simulated Madison AI crawler.
Work order data leaves the system in one versioned JSON format (schema_version 1, 13 fields including location and assets), published as an OpenAPI 3.1 contract at /api/v1/openapi.json.

Each outside system has its own API key with scopes, stored only as a sha256 hash and shown once at creation; keys can be revoked. Every access, allowed or refused, is audited without recording the key.
Outside systems appear in the audit trail as named API clients (e.g. 'Madison AI'); refused requests without a valid key appear as 'anonymous'.
REQ-040 is met through an API rather than direct database access, because direct database reads could not be audited per access as the Trust criterion requires.
Madison AI's actual integration spec, authentication method and credentials are not known; compatibility is proven only against the project's own published contract.
The STORY-011 brief says STORY-009 and STORY-010 are specified before it and should be reused, but both are Release 4 stories with nothing built; nothing from them was reused.

decisions.statement: Provide an audited read-only API instead of open database access.
decisions.rationale: Only an API can record every Madison AI data access in the audit trail and control which fields are exposed.

decisions.statement: Refuse the request (503) when its audit entry cannot be written.
decisions.rationale: The Trust criterion: no data access may happen without an audit entry.
decisions.evidence: server/api/clients.js (auditedRead); tests/madisonHttp.test.js (audit trail cannot be written)

decisions.statement: Generate the OpenAPI contract and the format checker from one field list.
decisions.rationale: The published contract and the actual responses cannot drift apart.

decisions.statement: Page with keyset cursors on (time, id) rather than offsets.
decisions.rationale: A crawl never skips or repeats a work order even while records are added.

decisions.statement: Use plain text matching for search because Node's built-in SQLite has no full-text search module.
decisions.rationale: FTS5 is not available in the bundled SQLite; matching is case-insensitive and treats % and _ literally.

limitations.statement: Search is substring matching, not ranked full-text search.
Work orders created in the same millisecond are ordered by id, not by creation order; paging is still complete and without repeats.
There is no script or screen yet for an administrator to create or revoke API clients; it is done through createApiClient and revokeApiClient.
The API is not deployed anywhere; it runs locally in tests and the demo.
There is no rate limiting on the API yet.
